situation: A student who clearly studied did poorly and is convinced they are just bad at this subject.

dims.SPEAKABILITY: Card 2's lines are blunter and more natural — "I saw it, and I am not going to pretend that makes this result sting any less" sounds like a real person, whereas Card 1's "Struggling right now means your brain is working on something hard" edges toward a motivational-poster cadence.
dims.SPECIFICITY: Both diagnose the fixed-ability trap well, but Card 2's "your brain was working hard, just on the wrong version of the task" and the studying-vs-mastering distinction cut more precisely into this exact failure than Card 1's slightly broader "strategy did not match the material."
dims.TIGHTNESS: Card 2 is leaner; Card 1's Commitment paragraph stacks three separate reassurances plus a neuroscience aside, which pads the punch.
dims.HONESTY: Card 2 names the uncomfortable thing more squarely — that reflexive reassurance "quietly signals you do not think they can handle the truth" — and its Force Level 2 questions force the student to actually walk through their process rather than just receive empathy.
